featureMarkdown: Burn data disc from files / folders
featureHtml: Burn a data disc from files and folders
notesMarkdown: ISO 9660 + Joliet + UDF bridge; UDF 1.02 by default, 1.50 to 2.60 on request (`--udf-rev`). With the Windows writer (the default) on real discs on one drive (LG GP60NB50), every file read back identical: a CD-RW, a DVD+RW, a DVD-R and a DVD+R (two sessions each on the DVD-R and DVD+R), and a dual-layer DVD+R holding 5.5 GB across both layers (Windows puts the layer break at half the data). A DVD-RW (Ritek) too, with one difference: Windows' writer formats a blank DVD-RW for overwriting before it writes, so it is never left open for more sessions (the burn says so when that was asked for); every file identical, also after writing it over past the part formatted first. On a second drive (Lite-On iHAS124), a data CD-R (206 MB, 497 files) read back identical

summaryHtml: ISO 9660 + Joliet + UDF bridge (UDF 1.02 by default, up to 2.60 with --udf-rev). Every file read back identical on CD-RW, DVD+RW, DVD-R, DVD+R, dual-layer DVD+R and DVD-RW (LG GP60NB50), and on a data CD-R (Lite-On iHAS124).

featureMarkdown: Disc copy (one or two drives, multi-copy)
featureHtml: Copy a disc (one or two drives, several copies)
notesMarkdown: Swap prompts between copies; audio CDs copied track by track. A mixed-mode CD (data track first, then audio) is copied whole with direct drive commands turned on, otherwise only its audio; done on one real drive (LG GP60NB50, copying a CD-RW to a CD-R and a CD-R to a CD-R). An Enhanced CD (audio session, then a data session) is copied whole with direct drive commands on; that copy has run only in the built-in drive simulator. The source audio is read with error checks and re-reads, and a copy stops before writing when sectors still read wrong
notesHtml: Swap prompts between copies; audio CDs copied track by track. An Enhanced CD (audio session, then a data session) is copied whole with direct drive commands on; that copy has run only in the built-in drive simulator. The source audio is read with error checks and re-reads, and a copy stops before writing when sectors still read wrong; real-drive reports welcome
summaryHtml: Audio CDs are copied track by track, with swap prompts between copies. A mixed-mode CD has been copied whole on one real drive (CD-RW to CD-R and CD-R to CD-R); an Enhanced CD only in the drive simulator.

featureHtml: Rip an audio CD to WAV, FLAC, MP3, Opus or AAC + .cue
notesMarkdown: Reads the real TOC and CD-Text; optional MusicBrainz track names, release year and front cover (Cover Art Archive). When MusicBrainz lists editions that name tracks differently, the rip stops before reading the disc and asks which edition you have. Files can go straight into a library folder (`Artist\Album (Year)\NN - Title` by default, or your own naming template), in several formats from one rip, with `folder.jpg` and a `.cue` per album; MP3 can be constant bitrate or VBR (V0-V9). `convert-audio` (and the app's Convert Audio tab) converts files already on disk, keeping their tags and cover. AAC uses the encoder built into Windows; FLAC, MP3 and Opus use the optional ffmpeg download (no encoder is bundled). Ripping has run on a real drive (LG GP60NB50): tracks from CD-Rs and a CD-RW burned by IgnisDisc came back identical to the source audio. Gap detection (INDEX 00 marks in the `.cue`, hidden audio before track 1, pre-emphasis) has been tested on the virtual drive only, not on a real disc with such gaps. The encoders and output formats are otherwise tested on the virtual drive only; the built-in FLAC decoder (used for burning) is also checked against files made by the official flac 1.5.0 encoder

notesMarkdown: Detects your drive's offset from a disc in the AccurateRip database; optional opt-in CUETools Database (CTDB) track and disc CRC-32 lookup (`--verify-ctdb`, off by default) that also repairs a rip from CTDB parity and keeps the fix only when AccurateRip then matches. On a real CD the CTDB check matched the database and its repair data matched IgnisDisc's own calculation; the repair has fixed a real rip with damage added afterwards (zeroed sectors, flipped samples) against the live database, confirmed by AccurateRip, but has not yet met a physically scratched disc

featureMarkdown: Archive Studio: span folders across discs
featureHtml: Archive Studio: span folders across discs
notesMarkdown: SHA-256 manifest on every disc; optional PAR2 recovery data (needs `par2.exe`) fills the space left on each disc, split over an inner, middle and outer zone with a copy of the volume descriptor in each; `recover` copies the files off a damaged archive disc and rebuilds them, also with sector 16, the first UDF anchor and one whole zone destroyed (tested on images). Optional cross-disc Reed-Solomon parity discs (`archive-stage --parity-discs <k>`, `archive-rebuild`, or Archive Studio) can rebuild up to k completely lost discs from the remaining discs in the set; tested on staged folders and the virtual drive only, not on real burned discs. An archive burn can also write a HEALTH.json and HEALTH.svg report, and `check-disc --compare` sets a later read against it; this has only been tested on the virtual drive, not run on a real drive

notesMarkdown: Requires `ffmpeg.exe` (the 1-click download). HDR movies (BT.2020 with PQ or HLG, as in 4K Blu-ray copies) are tone-mapped to standard range with FFmpeg's zscale and tonemap filters, which the 1-click build has; before 2026-11-26 they came out grey and washed out. The conversion was checked on frames of a 4K HDR10 film; no HDR movie has been put on a DVD yet. Long movies are compressed to fit: before converting, the DVD-Video screen reads each movie's running time and says whether they fit a 4.7 GB DVD at full quality, compressed (with the video bitrate and how it will look), only on a dual-layer DVD, or on no DVD at all (Burn is then off). When a 4.7 GB DVD would have to compress and a dual-layer DVD would keep a clearly higher bitrate, it offers both (for example 3,587 kbps or full quality for a 2 h 20 min film), and a burn is refused before converting when the disc in the drive is too small. Each film becomes a title with a chapter every 5 minutes, English subtitles from an `.srt` beside it (or generated with the optional subtitle tool; the DVD-Video screen shows each movie's subtitle source with *Choose .srt...* and *No subtitles*), and a title menu with a still from each film and Play / Play with subtitles buttons. The navigation tables follow libdvdread's structures and were checked with libdvdnav (mpv, VLC). Played on one stand-alone player so far, an Xbox Series X: a film with menu, chapters and subtitles on a DVD+RW, and two films on a dual-layer DVD+R played across the layer change. Discs authored before 2026-11-14 did not play there. The authoring options (autoplay, action after a film, chapter interval, subtitles, video quality, title menu, multi-page title menus beyond 8 titles, per-title chapter submenus, custom menu styling and background audio, and multiple audio or multi-language subtitle tracks per title) have been checked in the test suite only; no disc made with a non-default choice or these options has been burned or played in a stand-alone player yet

notesMarkdown: Optional 1-click download, nothing bundled: whisper.cpp 1.9.5 and its models, every file pinned by SHA-256 (`install-subtitle-tool`, or the button on the DVD-Video screen). On a PC with an NVIDIA GPU and driver 551.61 or newer it gets the CUDA build and the large-v3-turbo model (2.3 GB download). With an AMD or Intel GPU instead, integrated graphics included, it gets a Vulkan build of the same whisper.cpp source and the large-v3-turbo model (1.6 GB download): whisper.cpp publishes no Windows GPU build for these, so IgnisDisc's own GitHub workflow builds it, with a build provenance attestation. Any other PC gets the processor build and the smaller base model (160 MB). Measured on one PC, on an 86-minute animated feature with English dialogue, against its human-made subtitles: on an RTX 3090, 3.3 min from movie file to .srt (26 times real time) with a word error rate of 24.9%; processor build only (16-core desktop processor, base model), 3.4 min and 34.3%. Through the Vulkan build, speech recognition alone (from the extracted audio) took 18.1 min on Intel UHD Graphics 770 integrated graphics (26.0%), and 60 s on the RTX 3090 (26.1%; the CUDA build took 56 s on the same audio). The Vulkan build has not been run on an AMD GPU yet. The large model on that processor ran at 1.7 times real time (178 s for 5 minutes, about 50 minutes for this film), so the better model needs a GPU. The error rate counts wording the human subtitles shorten too; an invented place name was never heard right. The subtitles are machine-generated: check them before relying on them. `burn-dvd --generate-subtitles` ("Generate subtitles" on the DVD-Video screen) makes them for movies with no .srt beside them and puts them on the disc as its subtitle track. Authored end to end on the test PC from a 5-minute excerpt: the generated lines appear as the DVD subtitle track and on the menu's "Play with subtitles" button. A full-length film with generated subtitles was burned to a worn DVD+RW on one drive (LG GP60NB50, 2026-11-14), but the read-back check of that disc failed, so it is not counted as a good burn; no disc with generated subtitles has been played in a stand-alone player yet. Muxing the subtitle track needs a recent FFmpeg (the 1-click download): a 2021 build crashed on it

notesMarkdown: Single-layer BD-RE only, with the experimental direct writer (`--native`), on one drive (LG BP50NB40, USB): a new, unformatted BD-RE was formatted by the drive and written (6.6 GB), then written over twice (7.5 GB), and each time the read-back passed and every file hashed identical through Windows, files over 4 GiB included. With `--streaming` the drive wrote at 2.07x instead of 0.88x. BD-R, M-DISC BD-R, Blu-ray through the Windows writer, and every multi-layer disc (BD-R DL, BDXL 100 and 128 GB, which the direct writer handles in the drive simulator) have not been written on a real drive yet. Blu-ray discs are recognised (type, size, layers) and archive sets can be planned for them

notesMarkdown: `author-bdmv` and the *Blu-ray Video (BDMV)* mode of the DVD-Video screen make a `BDMV` + `CERTIFICATE` folder, or a UDF 2.50 `.iso`, without burning anything. Requires an `ffmpeg.exe` with the libx264 encoder: the 1-click download installs the full build, which has it (until 2026-11-26 it installed an LGPL build without libx264; Settings and `ignisdisc-cli tools` now say when the installed build lacks it), or give one with `--ffmpeg`. HDR movies (BT.2020 with PQ or HLG, as in 4K Blu-ray copies) are tone-mapped to standard-range BT.709 with FFmpeg's zscale and tonemap filters; before 2026-11-26 they came out grey and washed out. H.264 High profile level 4.1 with x264's Blu-ray constraints and AC-3 or LPCM audio; IgnisDisc then writes the 192-byte BDAV packets with arrival times, `index.bdmv`, `MovieObject.bdmv`, one playlist and clip information per movie (with the entry-point map), the `BACKUP` copies and `CERTIFICATE/id.bdmv`; subtitles from an `.srt` file or speech recognition become picture-based (PGS) tracks. AVCHD uses the 8.3 names (`.MTS`, `.CPI`, `.MPL`) and version 0100 files for DVD-R / DVD+R DL. Checked in the test suite with a separate binary reader of the format (file tags, address and length fields, packet arrival times, continuity counters, tables with CRC, playlist times against clip information, the entry-point map against the stream, subtitle segments) and by reading every file back from the UDF 2.50 image, on streams from FFmpeg and from a hand-built transport stream. Not tested on any Blu-ray or AVCHD player or with a real disc, and not written to a disc by IgnisDisc: no player compatibility is claimed. No menus, no AACS or BD-J, one video and one audio stream per movie, subtitles limited to the .srt text drawn by IgnisDisc, and the AVCHD private-data extension is not written

No menus, no AACS or BD-J, one video and one audio stream per movie, subtitles limited to the .srt text drawn by IgnisDisc, and the AVCHD private-data extension is not written
summaryHtml: Makes a BDMV folder or UDF 2.50 .iso (or AVCHD for DVD) from movies with FFmpeg, with .srt or speech-recognition subtitles. File structure checked in the test suite only; not played on any player and not burned, so no player compatibility is claimed.

notesMarkdown: Audio CDs Session-at-Once and data/video discs without the Windows writer (`--native` on the command line, or "Direct drive commands" in the app — on by default in the app for audio CDs, falling back to the Windows writer if the drive does not offer Session-at-Once, for dual-layer DVD-Video, and for a DVD-RW, in the app and with burn-data and burn-iso, where a quick-erased disc that cannot be left open still goes to the Windows writer (a Settings switch, or --windows-writer on the command line, turns the DVD-RW default off); off by default elsewhere); the disc is always read back and compared. Audio and DVD burns have run on one drive so far (LG GP60NB50) on CD-R, CD-RW, DVD-R, DVD-RW, DVD+R, DVD+RW and dual-layer DVD+R; a second drive (Lite-On iHAS124) has written one data CD-R this way (206 MB, 497 files, every file identical), and no DVD or audio disc. Mixed-mode CDs (a Mode 1 data track, then audio) from a `.cue` file too: a CD-RW, where Windows read the data track's files back identical, and a CD-R with the write-offset correction on (2,001 data sectors, then 78 minutes of audio, 2026-11-21): the table of contents, CD-Text, data track and every audio sample read back identical after a careful re-read of two sectors, and all 154 files hashed identical through Windows. A Mode 2 / CD-ROM XA data track (`MODE2/2352` or `MODE2/2336`) as track 1 has run only in the drive simulator, not on a real disc. Blank single-layer DVD-R, DVD-RW and DVD+R can also be written this way. A further session on a CD-R, CD-RW, DVD-R, DVD-RW or DVD+R left open is added the same way: on real discs on the same drive, three sessions each on a CD-RW, a CD-R and a DVD+R and four on a DVD-R, every file of every session identical (the first DVD-R try was refused with nothing written, because the drive rejects the writer's old track query on DVD; fixed before these runs); on a DVD-RW too, which must be fully erased before it can be left open: a second session added and the disc closed, every file of both sessions identical (Windows showed the new session after the disc was put back in). On real hardware so far two DVD-Rs on the same drive (Verbatim): one closed in one pass (372 MB), one left open, after which Windows' own writer added a second session; every file of each session identical when read through Windows. Two DVD+RWs too (Verbatim, 372 MB each, every file identical): a used one written over with leave to replace its data, and a new one, formatted first by the drive. A single-layer DVD+R too (Verbatim, 198 MB, finalized by the drive, every file identical). A DVD-RW too (Ritek): closed in one pass after a quick erase (63 MB; the drive took 6 minutes to close it), left open after a full erase (200 MB), and in overwrite mode written over past its formatted part, which the writer expanded first (230 MB); every file identical each time. A DVD-Video disc was written to a used DVD+RW this way too (a 60 s test card, 44 MB): every sector read back and the title decodes in full, this test card was not played in a stand-alone player (a later film disc was; see DVD-Video authoring). A dual-layer DVD+R too (Verbatim, the Ubuntu 26.04 image, 6.5 GB, with the layer break moved to where it was asked for; the drive reported it there and the disc's SHA-256 equalled the image). A two-film DVD-9 (103 and 86 minutes) went onto a dual-layer DVD+R the same way, with the layer break on the cell where the second film starts: every sector read back, the drive reported the break there, and an Xbox Series X played through the first film into the second across the layer change without a stop. On a third drive (LG BP50NB40, a USB Blu-ray writer) a single-layer BD-RE: new and unformatted, formatted by the drive and written (6.6 GB), then written over twice (7.5 GB, once failing on its last 64 KiB with streaming writes, fixed the same day); each finished run read back right and every file hashed identical through Windows. Dual-layer DVD-R (layer jump recording, on drives that offer it), DVD-RAM (a real-disc test will not be done: the medium is out of production), BD-R of every layer count and multi-layer BD-RE (dual layer 50 GB, BDXL 100 and 128 GB), leaving an audio CD open for a second data session (CD-Extra), that session's optional Blue Book layout (off by default: CD-ROM XA Mode 2 Form 1 with CDPLUS/INFO.CDP and PICTURES), the optional Audio CD PAR2 recovery session (`--recovery-session` / `rip-audio --repair`), and CD-R overburning (`--allow-overburn`) have run only in the built-in drive simulator, not on a real disc. Dual-layer DVD-R on a drive without layer jump recording still uses the Windows writer

Tested in the LG GP60NB50 on CD-R, CD-RW, DVD-R, DVD-RW, DVD+R, DVD+RW and dual-layer DVD+R, in the Lite-On iHAS124 on one data CD-R, and in the LG BP50NB40 on single-layer BD-RE. featureMarkdown: CD-Text / ISRC on burned audio CDs
featureHtml: CD-Text / ISRC on burned audio CDs
notesMarkdown: The Windows writer cannot write lead-in CD-Text. The direct writer (on by default on the Audio CD screen when the drive offers Session-at-Once, or `--native` on `burn-audio`) writes CD-Text, ISRC and catalog codes, then reads the disc back and compares it. Run on real hardware on one drive so far (LG GP60NB50): a CD-RW and a CD-R, where CD-Text, ISRC and catalog codes and the audio all read back correctly; not yet checked in a stand-alone CD player
notesHtml: The Windows writer cannot write lead-in CD-Text. The direct writer (on by default on the Audio CD screen when the drive offers Session-at-Once, or --native on burn-audio) writes CD-Text, ISRC and catalog codes, then reads the disc back and compares it. Run on real hardware on one drive so far (LG GP60NB50): a CD-RW and a CD-R, where CD-Text, ISRC and catalog codes and the audio all read back correctly; not yet checked in a stand-alone CD player
summaryHtml: The Windows writer cannot write CD-Text; the direct writer writes CD-Text, ISRC and catalog codes and reads them back. Correct on a real CD-RW and CD-R; not yet checked in a stand-alone CD player.

notesMarkdown: An opt-in setting (`book-type --get/--set`, `--book-type`, and a checkbox on the burn screens) that sends vendor commands only to drives on a built-in allow-list and otherwise reports "not supported". Run only in the drive simulator so far; never tried on a real DVD+R
notesHtml: An opt-in setting (book-type --get/--set, --book-type, and a checkbox on the burn screens) that sends vendor commands only to drives on a built-in allow-list and otherwise reports "not supported". Run only in the drive simulator so far; never tried on a real DVD+R
summaryHtml: Opt-in, allow-listed drives only. Run in the drive simulator only; never tried on a real DVD+R.

notesMarkdown: With the experimental direct writer (`--native --test-write`): the whole burn with the laser off. Run on one drive (LG GP60NB50) on CD-R and CD-RW. DVD-R has passed a test write on the same drive (a Verbatim DVD-R, still blank after a reload); DVD-RW only in the drive simulator so far; DVD+R discs have none. The Windows writer has no test write
notesHtml: With the experimental direct writer (--native --test-write): the whole burn with the laser off. Run on one drive (LG GP60NB50) on CD-R and CD-RW. DVD-R has passed a test write on the same drive (a Verbatim DVD-R, still blank after a reload); DVD-RW only in the drive simulator so far; DVD+R discs have none. The Windows writer has no test write
summaryHtml: A laser-off burn with the direct writer (--native --test-write). Run on a real CD-R, CD-RW and DVD-R; DVD+R discs have no test write, and neither does the Windows writer.

notesMarkdown: PAR2 remains the primary mounted-filesystem default; RS03 is opt-in (`ecc-rs03 create|verify|repair`, or checkboxes in Archive Studio and Disc Image Studio). Supports standalone `.ecc` files (safe for any image, including rewritable media) and augmented write-once `.iso` images with an explicit rewritable-media guard. Tested in the test suite and virtual drive only (including LBA 0-64 wipes and multi-track burst erasures), not burned or verified on a real disc; interoperability against upstream `dvdisaster` is not yet verified
